name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,810

entries.clue: Unionised workforce's failure inevitable, according to Spooner (4,5)

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so this asks for that swap

blocks.note: a failure is a flop; it gives up its FL sound and takes SH from its partner
inevitable means sure; it hands over its SH sound and takes FL in exchange

annotation.surface: A gloomy prediction that organised labour is bound to fail.
annotation.walkthrough: The shop floor is the part of a factory where the production workers are, and by extension those workers themselves, traditionally the union's base.
annotation.definitionFit: The shop floor is the body of workers in a plant, the people a union represents.

entries.clue: Indifferent Ringo at the back accompanying Help! (2-2)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
one piece goes along with, here after, the other

blocks.note: SOS is the distress call, a cry for help

annotation.surface: Ringo Starr turning in a lacklustre drum part on the Beatles album Help!
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make Help! look like the album title, but it is simply the distress call SOS.
annotation.definitionFit: So-so means middling, neither good nor bad.

entries.clue: Scream after at least a dozen balls go too far (9)

indicators.note: HOOT comes after OVERS in the answer

blocks.note: a cricket over is six balls, so two or more overs make at least twelve
a hoot is a scream, something hilarious

annotation.surface: A frenzied yell after a long spell of cricket bowling.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end; plural OVERS means at least two of them, hence at least a dozen balls.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an arrow or a budget that passes its mark has gone too far.

entries.clue: I sleep with nothing on, like Snow White (7)

indicators.note: in a down answer, 'on' puts FA on top of I REST

blocks.note: from 'sweet FA', slang for nothing at all

annotation.surface: A confession of sleeping naked, as the fairytale princess might.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing on' paints a nude sleeper, but 'nothing' is FA and 'on' just stacks it above I REST. The definition recalls the mirror's line: Snow White is the fairest of them all.
annotation.definitionFit: In the fairytale the magic mirror names Snow White the fairest of them all.

entries.clue: Seed half of cricket pitch, with time before the summer (9)

blocks.note: the off side is one of the two halves of a cricket field
spring is the season before summer

annotation.surface: Groundskeeping advice: sow half the cricket square before summer arrives.
annotation.walkthrough: A cricket field is split into the off side and the leg side, so OFF is half of it. 'Seed' reads as grass seed but means descendants.
annotation.definitionFit: Seed in the biblical sense means descendants, offspring.

entries.clue: Abundant clothes left in sack (5)

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so RIFE wraps around L

annotation.surface: Plenty of clothing stuffed inside a sack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun for the laundry in the sack; it is the verb, dressing L in RIFE. 'Sack' is the verb too, as in plundering a town.
annotation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack or plunder it, as to sack it.

entries.clue: A little parcel at Christmas fitting through the door (5)

indicators.note: only a little of the phrase is taken, a run of its letters

annotation.surface: A small Christmas parcel slim enough to go through the letterbox.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gift pushed through the letterbox; the definition is a door fitting whose bar passes through the door.
annotation.definitionFit: A latch is a fastening fitted on a door, often worked from outside by a bar through it.

entries.clue: Fuzz trimmed on top by pop star makes greyhound cross (7)

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off
the pop star stands next to, here below, the trimmed word

blocks.note: BLUR (a fuzz) minus its first letter

annotation.surface: A police officer and a singer somehow producing an angry greyhound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fuzz' looks like slang for the police, and 'cross' like an adjective for angry; fuzz is a blur, and cross is the noun for a crossbreed.
annotation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred dog, typically greyhound crossed with a collie or terrier.

entries.clue: Bites from bug, alas, on vacation (5)

indicators.note: vacating a word empties it, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: to bug a phone is to tap it

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker lamenting insect bites.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is mosquito bites on holiday; the bites are small Spanish dishes, and 'bug' is the listening kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Tapas are small savoury dishes, bites to eat with a drink.

entries.clue: Novel iron ship crosses without capsizing (7,3)

indicators.note: HARD SEND is laid across OW, holding it inside
to capsize is to turn over, so WO turns round

blocks.note: hard as iron; iron as an adjective means hard
to ship goods is to send them
W/O is the abbreviation for without; WO turned round

annotation.surface: An ironclad vessel crossing the sea without turning turtle, like an adventure yarn.
annotation.walkthrough: Howards End is E. M. Forster's 1910 novel. The whole surface is nautical, but 'ship' is the verb and 'without' is the abbreviation w/o.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: E. M. Forster's story of the Schlegel sisters is one particular novel.

entries.clue: Judge female guitarist's figure? (7)

blocks.note: a riff is a repeated guitar figure

annotation.surface: Someone assessing a woman guitarist's playing, or her physique.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' hints at a body shape; in music it is a short repeated phrase, a riff. In Scotland a sheriff is a judge in the local courts.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Scots law the officer presiding over the local court and passing sentence holds that title.

entries.clue: Supporting weight, primate flipped foot in front (7)

indicators.note: flipping turns APE over to EPA
'in front' is a position word, so the flipped ape is placed before the weight rather than after it

annotation.surface: A gymnast ape doing a handstand, taking its weight with a foot in front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foot in front' looks like the definition; only 'foot' is, as 'in front' places the flipped ape before W.
annotation.definitionFit: A broad term for a narrower one: any paw is an animal's foot, and this is one of the front pair.

entries.clue: Jumper affected teacher's sleep (13)

indicators.note: something affected is changed, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: A knitted jumper that disturbs a teacher's night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is British for a sweater, which is how the surface reads it; here it is a horse that jumps fences in a steeplechase.
annotation.definitionFit: A steeplechaser is a horse or runner that races over jumps.

entries.clue: Misleading surface of clue a game, shortly to be unravelled (10)

indicators.note: cut short, so GAME loses its last letter
unravelling undoes the order of the letters

annotation.surface: A self-referential note that a clue's surface is a game to be unpicked.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: a surface reading that disguises the wordplay is exactly the camouflage it defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Camouflage is a deceptive outward appearance that hides what lies beneath.

entries.clue: Nearly everyone frequently flying (5)

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A remark that almost everybody travels by air a lot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a statistic about air travel; 'flying' is the definition, as in a flag flying aloft.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a kite or bird up in the air overhead is both flying and high up.

entries.clue: Visiting sea-eagles east of very small Highland town (9)

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so ERNES follows V

annotation.surface: Birdwatchers visiting sea-eagles near a tiny Scottish town.
annotation.walkthrough: ERNE is a crossword staple for the sea-eagle. 'Very small' reads as one phrase describing the town but splits into V and S, with the eagles sitting east of V.
annotation.definitionFit: Inverness is the main town of the Scottish Highlands.

entries.clue: American term over with changes made around November (9)

indicators.note: the letters are changed round
the rearranged letters go around N

blocks.note: N is November in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An American phrase that has been altered around November.
annotation.walkthrough: A Vermonter is a native of the US state of Vermont.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: someone from the New England state of Vermont is one kind of American.

entries.clue: Inform closers for delicate negotiation, take pounds off? (9)

indicators.note: closers are the letters that close each word

blocks.note: taking pounds off makes something lighter

annotation.surface: Tips for a tricky negotiation, followed by a weight-loss suggestion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money in a negotiation; it is weight, so taking them off is to lighten.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shedding light on a matter for someone tells them about it.

entries.clue: Oxford University set off, rowing boat (9)

blocks.note: to trigger is to set off

annotation.surface: The Oxford crew pushing off in their boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the Boat Race, with Oxford setting off; 'set off' is the verb trigger.
annotation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a light racing rowing boat with the rowlocks on projecting brackets.

entries.clue: Endless sex bores couples, apparently (2,5)

indicators.note: something endless has no end, so the word is left without its final letter
to bore is to drill into, so SE goes inside ITEMS

blocks.note: a couple in a relationship is an item

annotation.surface: A cynical view that sex bores long-term couples.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couples' looks like the object being bored; it is ITEMS, the thing SE drills into.
annotation.definitionFit: 'It seems' works as 'apparently' at the head of a remark.

entries.clue: Cutting business, also changing name (5)

indicators.note: a word that is changing will not keep its letters in the order they are given

annotation.surface: A company making cuts and rebranding at the same time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting business' reads like a firm making cuts; it is a hairdresser's.
annotation.definitionFit: A salon is a hairdressing business, where hair is cut.

entries.clue: Beastly little sister carrying bag back from beach (7)

indicators.note: SIS carries WIN inside it
the back of BEACH is its last letter

blocks.note: to bag a prize is to win it

annotation.surface: A bratty little sister lugging a bag home from the seaside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bag back' tempts a reversal; 'back' belongs with 'from beach' and gives its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Swinish means like a pig, beastly.

entries.clue: Promising crisp commercial due to collect Oscar (13)

indicators.note: FRESH collects O, taking it inside

blocks.note: O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An upbeat crisp advert expected to win an Oscar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crisp commercial' reads as an advert for crisps (British for potato chips); crisp is the adjective fresh.
annotation.definitionFit: Foreshadowing means hinting at what is to come, promising it.

entries.clue: Celebrity demands free housing for ever (5)

indicators.note: the housing of a word is its outer shell, its outer letters

annotation.surface: A star insisting on free accommodation for life.
annotation.walkthrough: A rider is the list of demands a touring star attaches to a contract. 'Housing' tempts a container; here it is the case of EVER.
annotation.definitionFit: A rider is the clause listing a performer's backstage requirements.

entries.clue: A contrary stance for moralist (5)

indicators.note: contrary means the opposite way round

annotation.surface: A moralist being told to take the opposing position.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contrary stance' reads as an opposing view; it simply turns POSE round.
annotation.definitionFit: Aesop's fables each end with a moral, making him the classic moralist.

entries.clue: Bishop smuggled cases of grain (4)

blocks.note: to run guns is to smuggle them

annotation.surface: A cleric caught smuggling crates of grain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like crates; it means husks, the outer casings of the grain.
annotation.definitionFit: Bran is the husks, the outer cases, separated from grain.

entries.clue: Speak to tot on ship (7)

blocks.note: to tot up is to add

annotation.surface: An instruction to talk to a toddler aboard a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child; it is the verb, to tot up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as when a speaker addresses a meeting.

entries.clue: Gastroenterologist finally writes about American's terrible wind (7)

indicators.note: the final letter of the word
the letters are turned about, rearranged

annotation.surface: A gut doctor writing up an American patient's dreadful flatulence.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about digestive wind; the definition is a tornado, which Americans call a twister.
annotation.definitionFit: Twister is American slang for a tornado, a terrible wind.

entries.clue: Really regret returning boulangerie's bread? (5)

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: Someone deeply sorry about sending back bread to a French bakery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, and in a French bakery the money is euros; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money; the money spent in a French boulangerie is euros.

entries.clue: Greek building standard so concerning (9)

blocks.note: so = then, as in 'so, what next?'

annotation.surface: A Greek building whose ordinary standard is a matter of concern.
annotation.walkthrough: The Parthenon is the temple of Athena on the Acropolis in Athens.
annotation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the most famous building of ancient Greece.
